data.title: Bloomberg Intelligence's Mike McGlone Sees Bitcoin Near $10,000, Many Tokens Near Zero
data.description: Bloomberg Intelligence senior commodity strategist Mike McGlone said Bitcoin could move toward $10,000 and that most tokens without practical value could approach zero. According to Foresight News, McGlone wrote on social media that he believes an “everything bubble” is bursting. He said the crypto bear market since October 2025 could point to future declines across most markets, including U.S. stocks, gold, metals, commodities and Treasury yields, as part of a normal mean reversion. McGlone added that cryptocurrency may be heading toward an outcome similar to NFTs. He described about $10,000 as a reasonable gravitational level for Bitcoin that could curb unrealistic expectations that assets with unlimited supply will continue to outperform.

data.title: Tata Steel to Take 26.4% Stake in APL Apollo Tubes in $1.7 Billion Deal
data.description: According to Bloomberg, Tata Steel has agreed to acquire a 26.4% stake in APL Apollo Tubes for as much as 155.1 billion rupees ($1.7 billion), expanding its presence in India’s structural steel products market.

data.title: India's Nifty Gains as Global Stocks and Gold Post Rare Joint Selloff
data.description: According to Bloomberg, India's Nifty climbed while the S&P 500, MSCI's Asia gauge and gold each fell more than 5% last week.

data.title: Oil Long Loses More Than $19.76 Million in 20 Days, Still Holds $87.49 Million Position
data.description: A wallet that has been long crude oil for 20 days has more than $19.76 million in unrealized losses and continues to hold a position valued at $87.49 million. According to Foresight News, monitoring by @ai_9684xtpa found that the wallet holds the largest long positions in CL and BRENTOIL on Hyperliquid. Its BRENTOIL position uses 8x leverage, has an entry price of $99.45, and is carrying an unrealized loss of $9.646 million.

data.title: Binance Raises RWUSD Annualized Yield to 3.7%
data.description: Binance announced on X that the annualized yield on RWUSD has increased to 3.7%.

data.title: HSBC Australia Economist Paul Bloxham: Housing Market Faces Rare Test in Decades, Prices to Fall 13%
data.description: According to Jin10, HSBC Australia Chief Economist Paul Bloxham said there is good reason to believe Australia's current housing downturn differs from the cyclical declines common in recent decades. So far, prices have fallen further and faster than in previous downturns, while core inflation remains elevated despite substantial rate hikes this year. Rate cuts are not currently on the agenda, and tax changes and the possibility that global interest rates will remain high for longer are making the outlook more challenging. Bloxham expects home prices to fall 13% from peak to trough.

data.title: Arthur Hayes Says FLOP Labs Devnet Activity Rose Ahead of Testnet Launch
data.description:
Arthur Hayes said on X that activity on FLOP Labs’ Devnet increased ahead of the Testnet launch.

According to Odaily, the Devnet had a block height of about 4.4 million, a throughput of 47 TPS, an average block time of 1 second, about 11.595 million cumulative transactions, and about 1.8227 million FLOP locked.

data.title: Taiwan Stocks See Largest Leveraged-Bet Unwind in at Least 30 Years
data.description: According to Bloomberg, Taiwan stocks saw their biggest unwind of leveraged bets in at least three decades on Friday, helping explain why authorities’ efforts to stem the selloff in Asia’s most tech-heavy market have had limited impact.

data.title: Russia Allows Exchanges to Offer Crypto Trading; Moscow Exchange Targets Dec. 1 Pilot
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher, a Russian Central Bank directive took effect on November 22, allowing exchanges to organize cryptocurrency trading once regulators approve their trading rules. Exchanges must register participants, including brokers, trust managers and central counterparties, keep order and transaction records, and monitor trading. Trading cannot begin until venues connect participating brokers and receive Central Bank confirmation.

Moscow Exchange is targeting December 1 for a pilot covering Bitcoin, Ethereum and USDT. On November 2, it said assets would be added gradually based on participating institutions’ readiness. Trading will use stock-market infrastructure from 6:50 to 23:50 Moscow time, with clearing by the National Clearing Center, same-day and next-day settlement, and swaps available for liquidity management.

A separate rule effective November 17 limits non-qualified investors to Bitcoin, Ethereum and USDT, with annual purchases capped at 300,000 rubles through a single intermediary. All investors must pass a test and read a risk disclosure before trading. Qualified investors may access all crypto assets without the corresponding purchase cap.

data.title: PRECIOUS METALS | Gold’s 3,500 Level May Be Key Support as CTA Shorts Face Covering Risk
data.description: According to Jin10, a stronger dollar and a sell-off in technology stocks drove a sharp drop in gold prices, while gold’s fundamentals remained intact. The 3,500 level may provide important support, investment-bank strategic portfolios continue to view the sell-off as a buying opportunity, and increased short-term volatility could prompt CTA short covering.

data.title: ICICI Prudential Seeks Up to $800 Million for Alternative Funds
data.description: According to Bloomberg, ICICI Prudential Asset Management Co. is seeking as much as $800 million for private credit and special opportunities funds, people familiar with the matter said. The firm is tapping demand for alternative assets among wealthy investors and institutions.

data.title: BNP Paribas Sees Asia Support Measures Cushioning Stock Losses
data.description: According to Bloomberg, Jason Lui, head of APAC equity derivative strategy at BNP Paribas, says market support measures in China, Taiwan and South Korea may cushion weak sentiment and stock losses. He says longer-term investment returns face uncertainty from US data-center regulations and restrictions on remote access to chips.

data.title: China State Funds Set Record for ETF Buying as Selloff Deepens
data.description: According to Bloomberg, China’s state-backed funds made record ETF purchases on Friday in an effort to stem a deepening market selloff.

data.title: ASIA MARKET OPEN | KOSPI Opens 2.77% Lower, Taiwan Turns Higher After Weak Start, Japan Closed for Holiday
data.description:
According to Yonhap, HKET and UDN Money, Japan's stock market was closed Monday for the Labour Thanksgiving Day holiday and will reopen on Nov. 24. In the previous session on Friday, the Nikkei 225 closed down 5.06% at 56,436.65.

Seoul's KOSPI opened 135.06 points, or 2.77%, lower at 4,734.90, while the KOSDAQ opened at 634.93, down 10.75 points. Large caps declined across the board as investors sold technology shares, tracking Wall Street losses amid concerns over the artificial intelligence sector. As of 9:15 a.m. local time, Samsung Electronics fell 3.39%, SK hynix declined 2.34%, Hyundai Motor dropped 3.73% and Samsung Biologics lost 4.21%. The KOSPI stood at 4,685.46, down 184.50 points or 3.79%, as of 01:39 UTC, after falling 5.21% on Friday.

Hong Kong stocks opened lower, with the Hang Seng Index down 242 points at 22,168 and the Hang Seng Tech Index down 1.9% at 3,443. Alibaba fell 3% and Tencent dropped more than 2% to break below its previous low, while NetEase bucked the trend with a gain of nearly 2%. The Hang Seng stood at 22,100.51, down 310.29 points or 1.38%, as of 01:39 UTC.

Taiwan's TAIEX opened at 35,899.48, down 133.81 points, and losses widened to nearly 600 points, touching 35,442.41. TSMC opened at NT$1,990, below the NT$2,000 mark, then turned positive to climb back above NT$2,000, while UMC rose by its daily limit at one point and MediaTek opened higher at NT$3,355. The TAIEX stood at 36,160.19, up 126.90 points or 0.35%, as of 01:39 UTC. Taiwan's Financial Supervisory Commission banned short selling below the previous close across the board from Nov. 23.

In mainland China, the four major A-share indexes opened lower, with the Shanghai Composite down 0.86%, the Shenzhen Component down 0.98%, the ChiNext Index down 0.75% and the STAR Composite down 1.78%. The Shanghai Composite stood at 3,479.87, down 1.53%, as of 01:39 UTC. The Shanghai, Shenzhen and Beijing stock exchanges earlier lowered the minimum margin-financing ratio to 80%.

data.title: Ethlabs Forms Working Group to Promote Post-Quantum Adoption in Wallets and L2s
data.description: Ethlabs is forming an internal working group to promote post-quantum technology adoption in wallets and Layer 2 networks. According to Foresight News, Ethlabs researcher Derek Chiang said that post-quantum components in the Hegotá upgrade, including Frame transactions, leanSPHINCS and EIP-8288, could see limited real-world adoption if Ethereum core developers focus on technical development and overlook deployment in the coming months. The group will work with the Ethereum Foundation’s Access Layer team to help L2 networks transition to post-quantum technology using Ethereum-based solutions and develop wallet standards and tools that can be used across EVM chains. Ethlabs plans to commit significant resources over the coming months, with the goal of helping EVM wallets guard against quantum and AI threats while improving the user experience.

data.title: Vietnam's Nghi Son Refinery Secures Crude Supply Through January
data.description: According to Jin10, an executive at Vietnam's Nghi Son Refinery said the facility had secured crude oil supplies from Kuwait and other sources through January.

data.title: GIC Invested More Than $4.5 Billion in Anthropic Across Three Rounds, Source Says
data.description:
According to ChainCatcher citing TechCrunch, a person familiar with Singapore sovereign wealth fund GIC’s finances said the fund invested more than $4.5 billion in AI company Anthropic across three funding rounds and holds about 1% of the company following its listing.

GIC technology investment head Chris Emanuel said the fund first invested in Anthropic’s Series F round in 2025, then co-led its Series G round with Coatue and participated in leading a pre-listing financing. Claude Code had just launched and was already showing signs of popularity among developers, he said.

Investment manager Baillie Gifford invested a cumulative $1.5 billion in Anthropic across three rounds, the report said. Notable Capital invested about 10% of the U.S. investment allocation from one of its funds, which exceeds $1 billion, in Anthropic’s Series E round.

data.title: Crypto Liquidations Reach $252 Million in 24 Hours, Including $176 Million in Short Positions
data.description: According to ChainCatcher citing CoinGlass, crypto liquidations totaled $252 million over the past 24 hours, with $76.59 million in long positions and $176 million in short positions liquidated. Bitcoin long and short liquidations were $33.66 million and $99.22 million, respectively; Ethereum long and short liquidations were $16.15 million and $42.86 million.

data.title: predict.fun Gives Knicks 73% Chance to Beat Pacers as New York Seeks Fifth Straight Win
data.description:
The New York Knicks were seeking a fifth consecutive win against the Indiana Pacers in an NBA regular-season game. According to Odaily, predict.fun put the probability of a Knicks victory at 73%.

The game, part of the 2026-2027 NBA regular season, began at 9 a.m. today in New York. The first quarter was underway with the score at 13-16; the Knicks were reported to be temporarily ahead. Before the game, New York had a 10-6 record and ranked fifth in the Eastern Conference, while Indiana was 5-11 and had lost three straight.

The Knicks had won four consecutive games entering the matchup. In their previous game, they beat the Portland Trail Blazers 97-96 on a buzzer-beating three-pointer by Mikal Bridges. The Pacers had most recently lost to the Cleveland Cavaliers, 128-119.

New York started Jalen Brunson, Landry Shamet, Bridges, Josh Hart and Karl-Anthony Towns. OG Anunoby, Jordan Clarkson and Miles McBride did not play. Indiana started Andrew Nembhard, Kelly Oubre, Aaron Nesmith, Pascal Siakam and Ivica Zubac. Tyrese Haliburton, T.J. McConnell, Ben Sheppard and Johnny Furphy were out.

data.title: Emerging-Market Stocks Face Erasure of 2026 Gains Amid AI Selloff
data.description: Emerging-market stocks are set to erase this year’s gains as deepening concerns about the sustainability of the artificial-intelligence trade fuel selloffs from the US to Asia, according to Bloomberg.
